name: Sicilian Defense
thematic_ideas: Asymmetric fight for the center. Black trades a flank c-pawn for White's central d-pawn, creating an open c-file and queenside counterplay.
key_plans_white: Rapid kingside development, open d-file control, aggressive pawn storms (f4/g4/h4) or piece sacrifices on d5/e6.
key_plans_black: Pressure along the semi-open c-file, minority attack with ...a6 and ...b5, dynamic knight outpost on e5 or c4.
common_blunders: Delaying kingside castling too long; neglecting central king safety; falling for Nd5 or Nf5 knight sacrifices.

name: Italian Game & Giuoco Piano
thematic_ideas: Classical open game targeting the weak f7 square. White aims to control d4 and open lines against the uncastled black king.
key_plans_white: Build a central pawn duo with c3 and d4, or play quiet Giuoco Pianissimo with d3, c3, Nbd2-f1-g3.
key_plans_black: Counter-strike in the center with ...d6 or ...d5, pin White's knight with ...Bg4, maintain dark-squared bishop active on c5/b6.
common_blunders: Premature knight incursions before castling; allowing White a mobile d4/e4 pawn center; neglecting the f7 diagonal.

name: Ruy Lopez (Spanish Opening)
thematic_ideas: Indirect pressure on Black's e5 pawn by attacking its defender on c6. One of the deepest strategic openings in chess.
key_plans_white: Prepare c3 and d4, maneuver the bishop pair via Bc4/Bb3, reroute Nbd2-f1-g3, maintain lasting central pressure.
key_plans_black: Break the pin with ...a6, expand with ...b5, reinforce e5 with ...d6, anchor knight on a5 or d7.
common_blunders: Allowing the e5 pawn to collapse prematurely; passive bishop on e7 trapped by White's d4 thrust.

name: French Defense
thematic_ideas: Solid but slightly cramped counter-attacking structure. Black challenges d4 immediately while accepting a bad light-squared bishop.
key_plans_white: Advance e5 to lock Black's kingside, attack along the f-file, exploit space advantage.
key_plans_black: Undermine White's pawn chain with ...c5, ...f6, pressure the base pawn at d4 with ...Nc6 and ...Qb6.
common_blunders: Failing to activate the c8 light-squared bishop; allowing White a free mating attack on the h7/f7 squares.

name: Caro-Kann Defense
thematic_ideas: Extremely resilient pawn structure where Black prepares ...d5 without locking in the light-squared bishop.
key_plans_white: Gain space in Advance variation (3.e5) or build active piece play in Open variations (3.Nc3 dxe4 4.Nxe4).
key_plans_black: Develop bishop to f5 or g4 before playing ...e6, target White's advanced pawns with ...c5, reach favorable endgames.
common_blunders: Lagging in piece development; allowing White a devastating king hunt if Black plays ...e6 before developing the c8 bishop.

name: Queen's Gambit
thematic_ideas: Offering a flank c-pawn to establish a dominant classical pawn center (d4 and e4).
key_plans_white: Regain the c4 pawn with e3/e4 and Bxc4, control the c-file, execute the minority attack (a4-b4-b5).
key_plans_black: QGD: hold e5/d5 firmly with ...e6 and ...c6; QGA: surrender center temporarily to strike back with ...c5 and rapid piece activity.
common_blunders: Greedily trying to hold on to the gambited c4 pawn with ...b5; suffering from an isolated, blockaded d5 pawn.

name: King's Indian Defense
thematic_ideas: Hypermodern defense where Black allows White full central control, preparing a violent kingside pawn assault with ...f5.
key_plans_white: Expand on the queenside (c5, b4, Ba6), open the c-file, breakthrough before Black's kingside attack lands.
key_plans_black: Lock the center with ...e5, march f-pawn and g-pawn with ...f5, ...f4, ...g5, checkmate White's king.
common_blunders: Opening the center prematurely; defending passively on the queenside instead of pursuing the kingside mating attack.

name: English Opening
thematic_ideas: Flank opening fighting for the d5 square from the wing. Often transposes into reversed Sicilian or Catalan structures.
key_plans_white: Fianchetto the king's bishop (g3, Bg2), control light squares, expand with b4/a4 on the queenside.
key_plans_black: Establish a symmetrical formation (...c5) or grab central space with ...e5 and ...d5.
common_blunders: Neglecting central piece development while pushing too many flank pawns.

name: London System
thematic_ideas: Solid, universal setup for White developing the dark-squared bishop outside the pawn chain before playing e3.
key_plans_white: Anchor a knight on e5, support with f4, swing queen to h5/f3 for a direct kingside attack.
key_plans_black: Challenge White's bishop with ...Bd6 or ...Nh5, strike the center with ...c5, pressure b2 with ...Qb6.
common_blunders: Allowing Black's ...c5 and ...Qb6 to win the unprotected b2 pawn; playing automatically without adjusting to Black's setup.

name: Scandinavian Defense
thematic_ideas: Direct counter to 1.e4 forcing an open center on move 1. White gains tempos attacking Black's early queen.
key_plans_white: Develop rapidly with Nc3, d4, Bc4/Bf4, exploiting lead in development and open lines.
key_plans_black: Retreat Queen safely to a5, d6, or d8, set up a solid Caro-Kann-like pawn shell (...c6, ...e6), develop bishops cleanly.
common_blunders: Wandering with the Queen across the board while White develops all minor pieces.
